sources.citation: Bodt, Timotheus A. 2023. East Bodish revisited. Bulletin of Tibetology 54: 49-212.
sources.note: Passing geographic mention of Lakha and Brokkat speakers in upper Mangde/Bumthang valleys; nothing on Lakha phonology.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: an introduction to the family of languages derived from Old Tibetan. Villejuif: LACITO Publications. 1151 pp.
sources.note: Nothing Lakha-specific. Lakha = 'Säphuk pastoralists' dialect', S-section group 73 (pp. 555-556, 559-561): 'There is little available information and a general survey is needed about these three pastoralist dialects'; sec. 9.7.6 p. 561: S-section dialects 'generally have two distinctive pitch tones' but 'We lack data about the pastoralists' dialects'. Family-level sec. 7.3.3 Stress / 7.3.4 Prosodic patterns (pp. 241-243): trochaic strong-weak pattern 'attested in most dialects with a tonal distinction, such as Kham, Dzongkha and Sherpa' -- not stated for Lakha.

sources.citation: van Driem, George. 2007. South Asia and the Middle East. In C. Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 283-348. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 314, 334: Brokpas of Säphu Geo in Wangdi Phodr'a speak 'Lakha.. or Tshangkha', c. 8,000 speakers, Central Bodish, endangered.
